cultural.vision_reason: This is a strip-woven cotton gown (tobe/boubou) with indigo, white, and red checked strip weaving and embroidered chest panel — a classic West African men's robe form associated with Wolof and related Senegambian weaving traditions.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga): oblong shaped body with broad sleeves flared towards the top. Composed of 80 narrow strips, uniformly woven from strips with the warp of dark indigo-dyed handspun thread with threads of white cotton (also hand-spun) and wider stripes of red cotton imitating magenta ‘alaari’ silk; the weft is of indigo, crossed with lines of white thread to give a checked pattern. The same strips are used in both warp and weft. A pocket has been sewn to the front, and both front and back have been embroidered in a golden-white thread that appears to be rayon. The embroidery is in the ‘two knives’ (aska biyu) pattern, using chain and buttonhole eyelet stitch; there is a large spiral at the front and another on the back. The knives themselves are embroidered on top of extra pieces of cloth that have been cut to shape. The tunic is hemmed around the neck and sleeves.
